evidence: bp-node.lisp:384 `(setq socket (fnn-tcl-connect "127.0.0.1" hop-port))`. The queued-job path takes the host from ACL2's route (books/bp-route-jobs.lisp:40 `(list :route (fn-bprt-loopback) ...)`, read back by fnn-bps-route-host).
fix: Have fn-bpnp-forward-plan return the route's contact host (or fn-bprt-loopback), and dial what ACL2 names, as fnn-bps-send-effect-next does.
reviewer: bp-node.lisp:384 dials the literal "127.0.0.1". The queued-job path takes the host from ACL2's route via fnn-bps-route-host (bp-service.lisp:512), which today evaluates to fn-bprt-loopback = "127.0.0.1" (books/bp-route-jobs.lisp:29-31). Behaviour is identical today, but the host computes a value ACL2 also decides, which AGENTS.md forbids, and the forward path would diverge silently if routes gained real hosts. The SESS_INIT node-ID check makes it fail closed.
scenario: The host computes a value ACL2 also computes (the contact address), which AGENTS.md forbids. If fn-bprt-loopback or the route table ever grows a real host field (needed for remote neighbours such as a friend node on another machine), the forward path keeps dialling localhost:PORT. It would connect to whatever local service owns that port while base jobs go to the right host, and it fails closed only because of the SESS_INIT node-ID check.
title: Forward session hard-codes 127.0.0.1 instead of using the address ACL2's route names
